title: Set 41

sentences.ko: 현관문 자물쇠가 너무 뻑뻑해서 문을 통째로 들어올리고 열쇠를 흔들어야 열려. 어젯밤에는 비 맞고 밖에 5분이나 서 있었어. 누구 좀 불러서 봐 달라고 해 줄 수 있어?
sentences.text: The lock on the front door sticks so bad that I have to lift the whole door and jiggle the key, and last night it took me five minutes standing out there in the rain. Can you get somebody to look at it?

alts.text: That front door lock is so stuck I've gotta lift the whole door up and wiggle the key around, and last night I was out there in the rain for five minutes. Can you get someone to come look at it?

The lock on the front door is sticking badly, to the point where I must lift the entire door and jiggle the key. Last night it took me five minutes standing outside in the rain. Could you arrange for someone to look at it?

sentences.note: **sticks** 는 자물쇠나 문이 뻑뻑해서 잘 안 움직이는 것이고, **jiggle the key** 는 열쇠를 살살 흔들어 맞추는 동작입니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 알람을 두 개나 못 듣고 그대로 자 버렸어. 진짜 미안해. 옆집 사람이 또 내 차 막아 놨다고 말하려고. 실제로 자주 있는 일이라 아무도 두 번은 안 물어볼 거야.
sentences.text: I slept straight through two alarms and I feel terrible about it. I'm going to tell them my neighbor blocked me in again, and that does actually happen a lot, so nobody's going to ask twice.

alts.text: Both alarms went off and I didn't hear a thing, and I feel awful. I'm gonna say my neighbor blocked me in again, and honestly that does happen a lot, so nobody's gonna question it.
I slept straight through two alarms, and I feel quite bad about it. I intend to tell them that my neighbor blocked me in again, which does in fact happen often, so no one will ask twice.

sentences.note: **slept straight through** 는 알람이 울려도 안 깨고 쭉 잔 것이고, **blocked me in** 은 남의 차가 앞을 막아서 못 빼는 상황입니다.

sentences.ko: 소파는 상태 괜찮아. 왼쪽 쿠션만 좀 꺼졌는데 내가 늘 그쪽에 앉아서 그래. 뒤집으면 티도 안 날 거야. 그래도 계단으로 다 올린 다음에 알게 되는 것보다는 내가 미리 말해 주는 게 나을 것 같아서.
sentences.text: The couch is in good shape, except the left cushion sags a little because that's the side I always sat on. You can flip it and you'd never know, but I'd rather you hear it from me than notice it after you get it up the stairs.

alts.text: It's a good couch, just the left cushion's a little saggy since that's the side I always sat on. Flip it over and you'd never even tell, but I'd rather you hear it from me than find out after you haul it up the stairs.

The couch is in good condition, aside from the left cushion, which sags slightly because that is the side I always sat on. If you turn it over, it would not be noticeable, but I would rather you hear it from me than discover it after carrying it up the stairs.

sentences.note: **sags** 는 쿠션이나 천이 눌려서 축 꺼지는 것이고, **you'd never know** 는 말 안 하면 아무도 모를 거라는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 중고로 물건 팔면서 상태 솔직히 말하기

sentences.ko: 우리 집 침실 바로 위에 러닝머신 갖다 놓은 게 분명해. 매일 아침 6시만 되면 돌아가기 시작하거든. 한마디 해야지 하다가도, 그러고 나면 매일 엘리베이터에서 마주쳐야 하잖아.
sentences.text: I'm pretty sure they put a treadmill right over my bedroom, because it starts up at six every single morning. I keep thinking I'll say something, but then I'd have to run into them in the elevator every day after that.

alts.text: There's gotta be a treadmill right above my bedroom, cause the thing fires up at six every single morning. I keep telling myself I'll say something, but then I'd have to see them in the elevator every day after that.

I am fairly certain they have placed a treadmill directly above my bedroom, as it starts up at six every single morning. I keep thinking I will say something, but then I would have to encounter them in the elevator every day afterward.

sentences.note: **run into them** 은 길이나 엘리베이터에서 우연히 마주치는 것이고, **starts up** 은 기계가 돌아가기 시작하는 것입니다.

sentences.ko: 1월에 일본어 수업 등록해서 네 번쯤 갔는데 진짜 재미있었어. 그런데 일이 바빠지면서 한 주를 빠졌고, 그 뒤로는 다시 들어가기가 좀 어색하더라고.
sentences.text: I signed up for a Japanese class back in January and I went maybe four times, and I actually liked it. But then work got busy and I missed a week, and after that it just felt weird to walk back in.

alts.text: Back in January I signed up for a Japanese class and made it maybe four times, and I really did like it. Then work got crazy and I missed a week, and after that it just felt weird showing up again.

I enrolled in a Japanese class back in January and attended perhaps four times, and I genuinely enjoyed it. However, work became busy and I missed a week, and after that it simply felt awkward to walk back in.

sentences.note: **signed up for** 는 수업이나 모임에 등록하는 것이고, **felt weird to walk back in** 은 빠진 뒤에 다시 얼굴 내밀기가 어색하다는 말입니다.

reviewed: 2번 formal 의 "I feel quite badly about it" 은 과잉교정입니다. 감정을 말할 때는 "feel bad" 가 맞아서 "I feel quite bad about it" 으로 고쳤습니다.
2번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분이 거의 같았습니다("I ... slept through two alarms and I feel ..."). "Both alarms went off and I didn't hear a thing" 로 시작을 바꿔 말투 차이가 드러나게 했습니다.
3번 formal 의 "You may turn it over" 는 허락해 주는 말로 읽혀 두 가지로 해석됩니다. "If you turn it over, it would not be noticeable" 로 조건절로 바꿨습니다.
5번 note 가 별표로 감싼 **it felt weird to walk back in** 이 문장에는 "it just felt weird to walk back in" 으로 들어 있어 글자가 어긋났습니다. **felt weird to walk back in** 으로 맞췄습니다.
